rows.title: Policy divergence
rows.figure: BoC Oct 28 hike ~87% (from ~1 in 4 last week); RBNZ Oct 28 hike ~80%; BoE Nov 5 ~95%; Fed Oct hold ~84%, Dec hike ~83%; ECB Oct hold, Dec hike likely; BoJ Oct hold, Dec likely; RBA Nov ~1 in 3
rows.read: Canada and New Zealand jumped the queue: markets now expect both to hike next week, joining the Bank of England in November. The Fed, ECB and BoJ are still waiting until December. Currencies whose banks are about to act, like the loonie, kiwi and pound, have the rate edge for now.

rows.title: Growth differentials
rows.figure: UK unemployment 4.7% (fc 4.9%), employment +102K, claimant +30.3K (fc 19.4K); China LPR held 3.00%/3.50%; US housing starts 7:30 AM CT (fc 1.30M)
rows.read: Britain's job market turned out firmer than feared, which gives the Bank of England less reason to hold back. China kept its lending rates steady after its growth beat, so no extra boost is coming. In the US, housing is the weak spot, but it isn't changing the Fed's plans.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: German PPI +6.7% y/y (fc 6.2%, prior 4.6%), +1.9% m/m; Macklem: inflation to drift up from ~3% if oil ~$100; UK CPI Wed fc 3.4%; NZ Q3 CPI Wed fc 3.8%
rows.read: Energy is working its way through the system: German factory prices rose at the fastest pace in three and a half years. Canada's central bank now says it will act on where inflation is heading, not where it is today. That forward-looking stance is what moved rate bets this week.

rows.title: Risk sentiment
rows.figure: US official denies Konarak strike (Iran maintains claim; CENTCOM no comment); IRGC says Hormuz closed, CENTCOM says open; curfews in French cities; Asia FX calm
rows.read: Asia was calm. A US denial that it struck Iran took some heat out of Monday's scare, though Iran sticks to its account. France's unrest is still the main stress in Europe, so safe havens keep a floor without a fresh push.

rows.title: Terms of trade / commodities
rows.figure: Brent $109.55 settle Mon (-0.3%), ~$109.8 Tue; WTI Nov $103.66 (+2.2%), Dec ~$98; Gulf flows ~8.5m b/d (Kpler); gold ~$4,120
rows.read: Oil kept its supply premium because tankers still aren't moving through the Gulf at normal levels. That keeps helping exporters like Canada and costing importers like Japan and the euro area. It also keeps US yields high, which is weighing on gold.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 13: hedge funds strongly against CAD (sharply added), against EUR (added), against NZD (added), for AUD (trimmed; real money strongly against), against JPY (real money for), oil bets near weakest since 2015
rows.read: Hedge funds are betting most heavily against the Canadian dollar just as markets swung to expect a Bank of Canada hike, which leaves those bets exposed. They are also betting against the kiwi as hike odds there rise. In the yen and the Aussie, hedge funds and long-term investors disagree.

rows.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk
rows.figure: France–Germany 10Y gap ~147bp (+10bp Mon); France revenue vote Tue, Moody's Fri; UK budget Oct 28; US FY26 deficit $1.99T
rows.read: France votes today on the revenue half of its budget, with curfews in several cities and its borrowing costs at their widest gap to Germany in at least two weeks. A clean pass would ease pressure on the euro; a defeat would add to it. Britain's budget next week is the next fiscal test after that.
